entities.name: PMID:27515135
observations: 2016 Circulation preclinical study tested exogenous human haptoglobin or hemopexin during resuscitation of mice after 2 hours of hemorrhagic shock using RBCs stored 14 days.

entities.name: Scavengers reduce stored-RBC injury
observations: In mice resuscitated after hemorrhagic shock with 14-day stored RBCs, coinfused haptoglobin or hemopexin, but not albumin, improved survival and attenuated inflammation; haptoglobin also prevented hemoglobinuria and kidney injury.

entities.name: Haptoglobin
observations: Binds extracellular hemoglobin; exogenous human haptoglobin coinfusion in a mouse stored-RBC resuscitation model prevented hemoglobinuria and kidney injury.

entities.name: Hemopexin
observations: Binds cell-free heme; exogenous human hemopexin coinfusion improved survival and attenuated inflammation in a mouse stored-RBC resuscitation model.
